t: Analytic Search - Qx Control
d: What are the system requirements and how to use Analytic Search.
b: What are the system requirements and how to use Analytic Search. The primary requirement is that the camera supports ONVIF M and is equipped for People/Vehicle object classification. This functionality is controlled via a feature flag within the Qumulex Control software and requires the appropriate licensing to activate. For details on compatibility and pricing, contact Sales@qumulex.com. The initial step in this process is to enable the capability by activating the QXP-A License. Navigate to the Camera Tab , select Edit Camera , and scroll to the bottom of the page. Toggle on Enable Profile M Metadata , then ensure you click Save Camera to apply the changes. Step 1 is scope to the highest place in the hierarchy for your Analytic search, this can be narrowed from the Analytics menu later if applicable. Step 2 is from the Search Tab, select the Portrait icon at the top of the page. This is the new Analytics Page. On the Analytics page, there are several time-related options. You can begin a search from the current moment by clicking the Now button at the top of the page. Alternatively, use the Calendar function on the left side to select a specific date range. Additionally, you can adjust the search scope here to focus on a particular site or location. In the upper right corner, you'll find the Scaling slider , which adjusts the display based on your screen size. Use the sliding scale to make snapshots on the page appear smaller or larger, depending on your preference. To initiate an Analytic Search , click Add Analytic and select a type—Face, Human, or Vehicle. Depending on the make and model of the device, the same attributes may be classified under both Face and Human. To ensure comprehensive results, you can create a search for either category. In this example I am using the Human category, and I am searching for an individual with a Red - Top Color. I would then click Search From my initial search, the results include everything the camera classified as red or with a reddish tint. Several factors influence the camera's classification or may result in false positives. These factors include lighting conditions, the object's distance from the camera, and ensuring the device is running the latest and most optimized application from the manufacturer. In this scenario, the objective is to locate an individual wearing a bright red shirt. To increase the likelihood of finding relevant results, the initial filter was set to include items with a likelihood range of 1%–99%. To narrow the search further, the filter can be adjusted to focus on results within the 90%–99% likelihood range for red shirt matches. Select the Likelihood category marker and adjust the slider to 90% . Once updated, click Search to generate the new filtered results. With my new Search, I now see the individual in question. The final step in the search process is selecting a thumbnail to review the recorded video. Clicking on a result will open the video player on the right-hand side of the screen, which will begin playback from the moment the individual was detected. From here, you can continue browsing through thumbnails or conclude your investigation by creating a video clip for export or sharing. Operators can share search results with other Qumulex users by clicking the Share button at the top of the page. Copy the search parameter string to the clipboard and paste it into another browser's URL bar to replicate the previously performed search.

t: Bandwidth tips and tricks
d: bandwidth
b: Bandwidth tips and tricks The amount of bandwidth a Qumulex system uses for cloud uploads and remote viewing depends mostly on how the cameras are set up. The tips below reduce bandwidth without affecting the video you need. Camera stream settings GOP (I-frame interval): set the GOP to at least twice the frame rate, so a full I-frame is sent about every 2 seconds. Each I-frame captures the entire image and is much larger than the frames in between, so sending them too often wastes bandwidth. A GOP that’s too long can cause playback and storage issues. Most cameras default to a 1–2 second GOP. Second stream: enable a lower resolution stream on every camera (ex. 640 or 720 wide). Qumulex records the high resolution stream, but chooses the stream for live view dynamically. The lower resolution stream is used on mobile and multi-camera layouts, which greatly reduces bandwidth and improves the viewing experience. See Camera Best Practices for the recommended stream settings: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/camera-best-practices Motion settings Every event recorded is video that may be uploaded to the cloud. Make sure you’re only recording events that matter. Exclusion zones: if the camera supports them, exclude areas with constant, irrelevant movement, such as trees, flags or TVs. Detection zones: make sure the detection zone only covers what’s important. Each manufacturer offers different options, and some cameras allow more than one motion window. Sensitivity: adjust sensitivity for the size of the objects you want to capture. Check that the camera isn’t triggering motion when nothing important is happening. Night time: video noise in low light can trigger motion all night. Reduce sensitivity if needed, balanced against capturing what you need during the day. Cloud upload scheduling Qumulex lets you control how much bandwidth each Gateway uses for cloud uploads, and when. Without a Bandwidth Schedule, the Gateway sends data to the cloud in real time. If there isn’t enough bandwidth available, the data is queued and synchronized as bandwidth becomes available. To set a schedule, open the Network tab on the Gateway. For example, if the site’s internet is shared and busy during business hours, you can throttle uploads from 9 AM to 5 PM and let the Gateway use what it needs after hours. Related articles Camera Best Practices: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/camera-best-practices What ports do I open for my Qumulex Cloud Gateway?: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/ports-for-cloud-system

t: Camera Best Practices
d: Camera best practices
b: Camera Best Practices Following these settings before adding cameras to QxControl will prevent most connection, recording and live-view issues. Compatibility and firmware Ensure the camera is at least ONVIF Profile S conformant and that ONVIF is turned on in the camera. Some manufacturers ship it turned off. Some camera manufacturers use the full name, “Open Network Video Interface”, instead of the acronym ONVIF. Some cameras use a separate ONVIF user account. If so, create an ONVIF user with the same login you use to log in to the main camera, with Administrator access. Be sure the camera is on the latest released firmware for the make/model. Network and time It is best to have the camera on a Static IP, or a Reserved DHCP address. Synchronize the camera’s time. ONVIF authentication fails if the camera and gateway clocks are too far apart. Once Qumulex makes its initial connection to the camera, it automatically sets the Qx Gateway as the camera’s time server. If the camera’s time is too far off, that first connection fails, and the time must be set manually using one of the options below. Best option: set the camera’s NTP server to the IP of the Qx Gateway NIC the camera is connected to (usually the LAN). Alternative: use the camera’s “Synchronize with computer time” option. Streams Qumulex will usually enable and connect to a high and a low resolution stream from the camera automatically. For most cameras this requires no interaction. Use H.264 or H.265 encoding. If you use H.265, viewers need a browser that can decode HEVC. See: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/error-using-h265-video Enable a high resolution stream and a lower resolution stream (ex. 640 or 720 wide) in the camera, and enable both in QxControl under Edit Camera. It is best if both streams have the same aspect ratio for seamless transitions. The low resolution stream is often what’s used for live viewing, especially on mobile and multi-camera layouts. 10 to 15 frames per second on this stream is plenty for a smooth experience. There is no need to lower the frame rate on the high resolution stream, which is the one Qumulex records. Set the GOP (Group of Pictures) to at least twice your frame rate. Note that ONVIF measures GOP in frames, not seconds. Ex: If the camera is set to 15 FPS, the GOP should be 30. Disable any dynamic or “smart” encoding features. These vary by manufacturer and may be labeled Dynamic GOP, Dynamic Intra Frame, Dynamic Frame Rate, Smart Codec or AI Codec. They can cause gaps in recording and repeated reconnects. Motion and analytics Turn on motion detection in the camera. Some cameras ship with it turned off by default, and QxControl relies on the camera’s events to trigger event recording. Set up at least one motion window/zone within the camera. Keep constantly moving objects, such as trees, flags or TVs, out of the motion zone if possible. Check sensitivity at night. Video noise in low light can trigger constant motion, so reduce sensitivity if needed without losing the daytime events you need. Configure any analytics desired in the camera. Ex: Line crossing, intrusion, loitering, enter, exit, appear, disappear and face detection Related articles Camera Connectivity Tips: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/camera-wont-connect Bandwidth tips and tricks: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/cloud-recording-bandwidth-tips-and-tricks Devices with known Firmware requirements: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/known

t: Camera Connectivity Tips
d: There are 4 main things that can cause a camera to not connect to the Qumulex system.
b: Camera Connectivity Tips If a camera won’t connect to QxControl, or shows invalid credentials, work through the checks below in order. Most connection issues come down to one of these. 1. Username and password Verify the username and password in the QxControl camera configuration match what you use to log in to the camera’s web page directly. New cameras often don’t have a default username and password. Browse directly to the camera’s IP in your browser, or use Go To Webpage from within QxControl, and set one before connecting the camera. Some cameras use a separate ONVIF user account. If so, create an ONVIF user with the same login you use to log in to the main camera, with Administrator access. 2. ONVIF is turned off in the camera Some manufacturers ship cameras with ONVIF turned off. Some use the full name “Open Network Video Interface” instead of the acronym. If the camera has already been added, click Config and Go To Webpage in QxControl to open the camera’s web page and enable it. Some cameras also need ONVIF streams configured in a separate section from the camera’s normal stream settings. Check the manufacturer’s documentation for your model. 3. Camera time is not synchronized ONVIF compares the camera’s time to the gateway’s time and fails authentication if they’re too far apart. This often shows up as an invalid credentials message. Once Qumulex makes its initial connection, it automatically sets the Qx Gateway as the camera’s time server. If the time is too far off for that first connection, set it manually: Best option: set the camera’s NTP server to the IP of the Qx Gateway NIC the camera is connected to (usually the LAN). Alternative: use the camera’s “Synchronize with computer time” option. 4. Gateway network is not on the camera network The Qx Gateway must be on the same network as the camera, through either its WAN or LAN port. If your cameras are on the same network as the WAN port, confirm the camera’s IP address is in the same range as the WAN. If you are using the LAN port for an isolated camera network: Both ports are set to DHCP from the factory, and an isolated camera network often has no DHCP server. Set a static IP on the LAN port that matches the camera network. Don’t add a default gateway on the LAN. See: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/qxgateway-static-ip 5. Camera compatibility or firmware Confirm the camera is at least ONVIF Profile S conformant by searching your model at https://www.onvif.org/conformant-products/ Compare the firmware version ONVIF lists as tested to the firmware on your camera, and update if needed. Check the known firmware list: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/known Still not connecting? Contact Qumulex Support at support@qumulex.com with the camera make, model, firmware version and a screenshot of the error. Related articles Camera Best Practices: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/camera-best-practices What camera models do you support?: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/what-camera-models-do-you-support

t: Camera Health Report
d: What is the camera health report and how to best use it.
b: What is the camera health report and how to best use it. The Camera Health Report provides Administrators with accurate insights into Gateway Data Retention, Cloud Retention, and Camera Motion Events. Step 1: Access the Report From the Reports Tab Click on Camera Health Clicking on Generate Report will produce a report on the current camera health. This report is location-specific, so before generating it, ensure that your scope is appropriately narrowed down or broadened to include the desired area. The QxControl Interface offers several sorting options. Data can be organized by Camera Name, or, using the menu on the right side of the page, you can filter results to focus on a specific Gateway or individual camera(s). Explaining Column Definitions: Cloud Storage Days: Displays the camera's cloud recording settings. If set to "0 days," there is no active cloud recording subscription. A populated number indicates an active subscription, e.g., "7 days" means 7 days of cloud storage is available. Last Motion At: Indicates the timestamp of the last motion event received from the camera. If certain cameras are significantly outdated compared to the majority, investigate potential issues such as disconnection events, online/offline status, or motion settings. Adjusting sensitivity or masking settings may resolve these discrepancies. Newest Disk Media: Shows the most recent recording event stored on the Qx Gateway. Oldest Disk Media: Displays the earliest recording event for the camera on the Gateway, representing the total retention period available on the Qx Gateway for that camera. An alternative option is to download the report as a CSV file. This allows you to modify and sort data using tools like Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets. For larger sites where managing data via the web interface may be challenging, this approach provides an effective solution.

t: Creating a Camera Disconnect email alert in Rules
d: The most efficient way to create alerts for camera disconnects on a server is to leverage the power of our Places. In the following Knowledge Base we will create a rule that will email whenever a cam
b: The most efficient way to create alerts for camera disconnects on a server is to leverage the power of our Places. In the following Knowledge Base we will create a rule that will email whenever a camera from a certain site loses connection for more than 60 seconds. First, be sure to set your Scope to the relevant Place for which you are making the rule. In the example below I am making this rule for any cameras within Josiah Security Co. (To set scope see KB HERE) Browse to the Rules section below Configuration and click the "Create Rule" button on the top. Give the Rule a "Name" and a "Description" so you can easily identify it in the future. Select the Schedule for this rule. In most cases it will be "Always". If you need this rule to only execute during specific times you will need to create a custom schedule first. Please cancel this configuration and refer to the Schedules KB for assistance there. Now we need to add the Triggers that will cause our notification to occur. Select Add Condition Here the What will be "Type", leave the Operator "is equal to", and the Value will be "Device Connection", Finally be sure to click the green "Create" button. We will now add a second condition. What will be "Status, Operator will be "is equal to", and Value will be "Disconnected". Click the "Create" button on the bottom. The above configuration says that anytime a Device Connection says Disconnected, we will trigger this rule. Now we are going to add a Guard to help avoid getting notified on momentary connection blips. Click Add Guard. Here we will set the Amount of Time Delay to "60" seconds (for the example) Now we need to tell the system what to watch for in those 60 seconds that will prevent our rule from firing. In this example we want to prevent firing if the camera connects within 60 seconds of the disconnect. To do this we essentially put the inverse of our trigger rule. Click add Condition. What is "Type", Operator is "is equal to", Value is "Device Connection". Then click Create on the condition Then we add our next condition. What is "Status", Operator is "is equal to", Value is "Connected". Then click Create on the condition Finally click Update on the Suppression Guard Our final step is to create our Action we want to happen when the above occurs. Click Add Action and in our case we will choose Email Notification. You can also get SMS or Webhooks to trigger based on the rule if you choose. Next we will type in the email address(es) that we would like notified. Start by typing in the first one. If this email is associated with an existing user on the system it will show in the dropdown and you can click directly on it. If not, complete typing the email and click on the row below displaying that address. Now we will build the email that will be received. Type the Subject line in under Subject. This is a free form box, we suggest giving it a subject that is easily identifiable. Then add the Body of the email. Here you can be a little more verbose. Example: "A camera at Josiah Security Co. has been disconnected for more than 60 seconds. Please check." Finally we can assign a Rate Limit Override. This limits how often the email can be sent. The main goal is to avoid a rapidly repeating trigger condition from spamming your inbox. You can choose what, if any, rate limit you would like to add. Click Update to save the above changes Finally click Create Rule at the bottom of the page, and your rule is active and ready to go!

t: Creating a Rule
d: Rules, Create Rule, Automation
b: For a quick overview of what Rules are, check out the following Knowledge Base . First ensure you are at the scope in which you want the rule configuration to reside. To create a rule, navigate to the left hand menu and select Rules from the list. Once you have that page open you can click the Create Rule button on the top to start the process. Then follow these steps. Give your rule a Name and a Description. This will ensure that you are able to easily identify them in the future, the more detail you put here the easier it will be later. Choose the Schedule for your Rule QxControl comes with a "Never" and an "Always" schedule by default. You will also see any custom schedules you have already created in the Schedules section of QxControl previously. In many cases Always will be the proper choice. Next you will set your triggers. These define the combination of things that need to happen to execute your Action: Notification Adding a Trigger Click Add Condition Choose the What from the dropdown list. This can be any of the items listed: Then choose the Operator from the list (most often "is equal to") FInally choose the value related to the choice under What. For example if you chose "Status" from the What menu, you might choose "Locked Down" for your Value. Meaning that this particular trigger is "When Status has the value of Locked Down". In some cases you may add more than one trigger. When you do this ALL trigger conditions must be met to execute the action. Example: I want an email when Cardholder Joe Smith swipes his card at the front door, is authenticated successfully. Person - is equal to - Joe Smith Door - is equal to - Front Door Status - is equal to - Authenticated The next step you may choose to add is a Guard . A guard will prevent the execution of the rules action if certain conditions occur within the timeframe given. For example if I wanted to have the above for Joe Smith, unless he badges out within 2 minutes, I could do this here by making the delay as 120 seconds and the condition for the user badging through the Out door. Finally we want to add our Action . Actions are executed once the Rule is triggered based on the prior Rule configuration. Currently These are Notifications Choose one of the options within Add Action Once chosen you will be presented with configuration appropriate for the type of Action you have chosen. For Example Email. When you choose this you will be able to add one or more email addresses to the notifications list. If the person is added already to the People section of QxControl with an email, it will autodropdown when you begin typing. Otherwise you can simply type the entire name out and click on the confirmation result. Then you will define a Subject and a Body for the email. This can be completely free form, or you can use the Add Data button to insert dynamic data. These are segments of data that the software fills in automatically based on the state of the system at the time of the event. Example: Camera Name, Time, Place, etc. Once that is set you can create a Rate Limit Overried if you would like. This will prevent the action from occurring more than once durign the duration specified. By defualt the value is 60 seconds Finally select Update on this section. The final step is to click Create Rule at the bottom of the page.

t: Does QxControl integrate with Microsoft Entra
d: Single Sign On
b: Does QxControl integrate with Microsoft Entra? Yes. A customer account in QxControl can require Single Sign-On (SSO) with Microsoft Entra as the sign-in provider. People and Groups can also be synchronized from Entra into QxControl. Roles and access credentials can optionally be synchronized as well. For full setup instructions, see the Microsoft Entra Setup Guide : HERE What it does Single Sign-On: users sign in to QxControl with their Entra account. Password rules and multi-factor authentication are managed by your organization in Entra. People and Groups sync: users and groups in your Entra tenant are created in QxControl, and group membership is kept up to date from Entra. Optional Role, Credential and Group sync: using Entra custom security attributes, you can also sync each person’s QxControl Role, card numbers, and additional QxControl Groups. How users sign in Go to app.qumulex.io and enter your Entra User Principal Name in the email field, then click Next If you’re already signed in to Entra, you go straight into QxControl. If not, you’ll be taken to the normal Entra sign-in page, including any 2FA your organization requires. Each user accepts the End User Terms Agreement the first time they sign in Who does what Integrator: creates an Administrator user at the customer’s Place, using the customer’s Entra User Principal Name as the email. The integrator then selects Setup SSO from the Single Sign On menu at the customer’s Place. Customer: signs in and grants QxControl permission in their Entra tenant. If they want to sync users and groups, they select Setup Sync and then Sync People and Groups from the Single Sign On menu at the top of their Place hierarchy. The sync must be set up by a user from the customer. The integrator cannot do it on their behalf. Good to know Synced People are created without a Role or credentials , so they can’t log in or open doors using the app until one is assigned, either in QxControl or through Entra attributes. Synced People and Groups are created at the top Place of your hierarchy. You can move them lower as you build out your Places. If a user is deleted in Entra , their QxControl Role is set to None, and their credentials are expired. Their record is kept for history. If a group is deleted in Entra , it’s deleted from QxControl also, which may affect door access for its members. Entra controls group membership for synced people. A group added by hand in QxControl will be removed on the next sync. To make it stick, set it in Entra. Related articles How does the QxControl login process work?: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/how-does-login Using Groups: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/using-groups

t: Event scroller best practices
d: The Event Scroller in Qumulex allows you to dedicate a panel (or more than one) within the live view to show you the most recent events from a filtered list of devices. This is most commonly used for
b: The event scroller shows a list of the most recent events on your system. Understanding exactly how it works will help you get the most out of it. The Event Scroller in Qumulex allows you to dedicate a panel (or more than one) within the live view to show you the most recent events from a filtered list of devices. This is most commonly used to show events coming from devices such as Doors or Cameras in a live scrolling stream for monitoring. Once the stream is running in live mode, you can mouse over it to pause. If the event has an associated camera/video, you will be able to playback the clip recorded, or show the live video from that camera directly from the scroller. Please note that there are a finite number of rows (over 200) that the scroller can cache. Once it reaches the limit, it will cycle out the oldest entries with the newest. Below is a video and the steps to build an example Event Scroller for Doors. Navigate to the Live page within QxControl Expand the side menu and scroll down to click the Other Category Drag the Event Scroller (Beta) into the desired panel on the left Click Select Saved Filter and Create New You will then be sent to the Search page to build your filter. The logic in building an Event Scroller Filter is the same as doing a normal search. It will ask you to create a unique name for this filter (such as Door Events) Choose the type of events you want to see. Door Events, or Camera Events. If you simply choose Door Events, for example, your Event Scroller will show you every message that comes from every door within your scope. Most likely, you will want to add additional filters to ensure that the Scroller has only useful information by choosing which doors (or cameras) you want included, and perhaps only showing specific messages when they come through. In the video above, I chose to show Door activity, and then narrowed that to only when Access was Denied or Granted. This helps keep my Event Scroller from being spammed with messages I do not need to know about. You may choose different detail levels. Once you have adjusted your filter, you should click Search on the bottom left to ensure that the data you see in the search matches the kind of data you wish to see in your event scroller. If you are satisfied there, then click on the Filter button on the top right and find the named filter you added. Click the 3 dots menu to the right of that name and select Update You will now be able to navigate to live and select that filter from the dropdown!

b: If you would like to see your QXOP on-premises gateway from outside the local network, you will need to setup the following. Be sure that the ethernet connecting to the outside world (internet) is using the WAN port on the Gateway. Ensure that the router's public-side TCP port 20824 and 20825 is forwarded to to the gateway's local/private IP. If possible on your router forward 20824 directly to 443 on the Gateway's IP. b: The best way would be to stage the Qumulex Gateway in your office temporarily. All the unit will need for configuration is a valid active internet connection via ethernet. t: How do passkeys work in QxControl
d: Passkeys are a replacement for passwords. A password is something that can be remembered and typed, and a passkey is a secret stored on one’s devices, unlocked with biometrics.
b: Passkeys are a replacement for passwords. A password is something that can be remembered and typed, and a passkey is a secret stored on one’s devices, unlocked with biometrics. See https://fidoalliance.org/passkeys/ for background information on passkeys. What are Passkeys? Passkeys are a type of login credential that allow you to log in to sites and services without having to enter a password. There’s nothing to remember and you can use them with the devices you already own like your smartphone or laptop. Passkeys are built on the WebAuthentication or WebAuthn standard which uses public-key cryptography to better secure your accounts. With passkey, you have a private and public key, and while the public key stays on a server, the private key remains on your device. What devices support Passkeys? Both iOS 16 and Android 14 or higher support Passkeys natively. And as of June 2024, storing a passkey on a Windows computer requires Windows 11. Windows users can log in to QxControl with a passkey created on their iPhone or Android mobile device. As for your web browser, Chrome, Edge, Safari and Firefox all currently support passkeys. You need to be running version 79 or higher for Chrome/Edge, version 13 or higher for Safari and version 60 or higher for Firefox. How do I set up Passkeys with Qumulex? Once you have logged in for the first time using the standard password method navigate to the left hand menu and select Settings. From there choose Authentication. t: How does Qumulex Billing work?
d: Billing Plan: Qumulex employs a Tiered Fixed Fee (also known as scheduled/flat rate) billing model. Users are billed a regular amount (per device) at a regular interval (monthly or annually). Monthly
b: Billing Plan: Qumulex employs a Tiered Fixed Fee (also known as scheduled/flat rate) billing model. Users are billed a regular amount (per device) at a regular interval (monthly or annually). Monthly Subscription Service: Users purchasing monthly service will be billed on the first day of each month for the current month’s service (in advance) based on device count on-line at that time. New devices added during the month will not be billed until the following (first full) month. Effectively, subscription fees for newly added devices are waived for the first partial month the device is registered, giving integrators the opportunity to stage and commission customer deployments prior to billing. Any changes to levels of existing service, i.e.-a device registered for 7 day storage is upgraded to 14 day storage, will be billed at the first of the month following the date the change is made (although the retention policy will be effective immediately). Devices deleted during the month will be removed from billing at the first of the month following the date the change is made. Annual Subscription Service: Annual subscribers will be billed the annual fee effective the first of the month following sign-up (the anniversary date) and billed annually for renewal. Additional devices added during the subscription period will be billed at the first of the month following the date the device was registered and pro-rated to the renewal date of the annual subscription so that all registered devices renew annually on the same date. Any changes to levels of existing service, i.e.-a device registered for 7 day storage is upgraded to 14 day storage, will be billed at the first of the month following the date the change was made and prorated to the renewal date of the annual subscription (although the retention policy will be effective immediately). If a device is deleted during the term of the subscription, it will be removed from the active device count at the first of the month following the date the change was made but the subscription billing will not be credited. New devices added subsequently will not be added to the subscription billing until the device count exceeds the total number originally billed. For example: A customer might buy 20 annual device subscriptions, delete a device midway through the subscription period, but subsequently add another device. As long as the total number of registered devices does not exceed 20 (at that configuration), no change will be made to the subscription billing. Billing Reports: Billing will be based on the number of registered devices reported by QxControl. Detailed reporting will be produced to show the number of devices registered (by product part number) to each end-user account/location per Dealer. Additionally, reporting will show units added/deleted/upgraded during the billing period.

t: How does the QxControl login process work?
d: QxControl login uses Google Firebase for authentication and the user database for authorization
b: QxControl login uses Google Firebase for authentication and the user database for authorization Qumulex uses Google Firebase to provide user authentication for QxControl software, whether QxControl is deployed on-premises or in the cloud. This means that there are no default passwords, no passwords stored on on-premises, and no one other than the user ever knows the password. Logging in to QxControl is a two step process: Authentication via Firebase Authorization via QxControl user database Authentication - When a user logs in to the QxControl web app, they can choose to login using email/password authentication or via a third party authentication provider like Google. Let's look at the email option. When a user creates a new account, Firebase verifies the email address and stores an irreversible hash of the user's password. When a user attempts to login, the email address and password entered by the user are sent over a secure https connection to the Google Firebase cloud service. If the hash of the incoming password matches the stored value, the user is authenticated. Firebase sends the user's email back in a trusted, signed, industry-standard format called a JSON Web Token (JWT). Because the token is signed, it can not be modified, so we can be sure that the email address contained in the token is "owned" by the user who is attempting to login. If the hash of the incoming password does not match the stored value, Firebase returns an error, and QxControl displays a message indicating that the email/password combination is not valid. Now let's look at the "login with Google" option. This process will be the same for any third party authentication provider added to those available in QxControl. Rather than the user entering an email and password, the user logs in to the third party authentication provider in their browser (or they may already be logged in). By virtue of that login, a token containing the user's email and signed by the third party authentication provider is sent to Firebase. Firebase validates the token, extracts the user's email, and the process proceeds identically to the email/password case. Authorization - With the trusted email address contained in the token received from Firebase, QxControl searches its user database - in the cloud for QxCloud systems or on the gateway for QXOP systems - to find a user with a matching email. If found, and that user has been assigned a role in QxControl, the login completes and the user is presented with the QxControl interface appropriate for the user's role and place. If a user matching the trusted email address is not found, or the matched user has not been assigned a role, the login fails and the user is presented a screen informing them they are not authorized.

t: Invalid Auth Response
d: invalid Auth Response
b: If you click Sign in with Google on the QxControl login page and a red banner reads Invalid auth response: Google , the sign-in is being blocked by stale data your browser has saved for app.qumulex.io. Trying again, or trying different sign-in methods, will usually show the same error until that saved data is cleared. The error as it appears on the QxControl sign-in page (iPhone, Safari). Why this happens When you sign in with Google, Google sends a sign-in response back to QxControl, which checks it against information your browser saved when the login started. If the browser is holding old cookies or a cached copy of the login page from an earlier session, the two don't match and QxControl rejects the response. Your Google account and your QxControl user are usually fine. How to fix it Desktop browser (Chrome, Edge, Safari, Firefox) Open your browser's settings and clear cookies and cached data for app.qumulex.io . Clearing only this site is enough; you don't need to clear your whole browser history. Close the tab, open a new one, and go to app.qumulex.io . Click Sign in with Google again. Phone or tablet If you are using the QxControl app installed on your home screen, pull down from the top of the screen to force a refresh, then try signing in again. If that doesn't work, open your phone's actual browser (Safari or Chrome), go to app.qumulex.io , and do a full refresh of the page before signing in. If the error still appears, clear the browser's cookies and website data for app.qumulex.io. On iPhone: Settings › Apps › Safari › Advanced › Website Data , search for qumulex , and remove it. Then sign in again. Tip: Clearing site data signs you out of QxControl on that browser only. Other devices and other users are not affected. Still not working? Try signing in from a private / incognito window. If that works, the problem is still saved data in your normal browser window. t: LP1501/02 Connection Troubleshooting
d: LP1501, LP1502, Connection
b: Pointers to look for when seeing bad board behavior. See Setup Guide and Mercury Panel Initialization Guide first to ensure configuration took place, and dipswitches are set accordingly. Mercury Panel Initialization - https://www.qumulex.com/kb/qxep If the Controller board is stuck in this state, the LP1501/02 is having connectivity issues. Follow these steps to remedy. Ping the IP on configured for the board, perform this from a PC on the same network as the device. If no reply, then confirm the device has been programmed to match the Gateways IP scheme, a quick way to check is match the PC to the default subnet of 192.168.1.x and try to ping 192.168.1.251. If it replies back on that IP then the device is still on the factory IP. If the board pings on the programmed IP matched to the gateway's IP Schema for the LAN or WAN port, but is showing offline still.. Check to make sure Places have been set for the 'To' and 'From' of the door config. Check that a Group exists for the door that are part of that controller. Check to make sure Permissions exist for the doors that are part of the controller. Without a complete configuration, the board will appear offline, until this piece is successfully pushed to controller. In some rare cases a full memory wipe has proved to bring problematic boards back on line and acceptance of the field tech defined IP. Or in cases where the web page is responding very slowly or not at all, even trying different browsers. Follow the Bulk Erase Steps Below. Bulk Erase Configuration Memory If the LED's do not initially follow this sequence, i.e. LED 1 pulsing steadily but nothing else.. power off for 30 seconds and attempt again. MR52 Troubleshooting (LP1501 Serial and LP1502, LP2500, LP4502 SIO connections / Mercury Inventory) The picture above shows a successful board connection with the Gateway. With your respective Controller board in this state, you know the Controller is talking but the is a break in communication between the Controller and down stream SIO modules. One of the issues will be the link light on LED 'B' Will be off. (See Picture Below) This indicates no communication back to the controller as pictured below. Some possible causes could be: Dipswitches SIO Wiring / Termination Power The SIO 485 Bus will start at the controller and daisy chain to each MR52 in the door kit, with the last one being terminated. From my own internal testing the last board does not require termination if all boards are in the same enclosure. Only in cases where the boards are spaced out across a building and several hundred feet of SIO 485 cable exists, termination of the final SIO module would need to take place. To terminate the End Of Line, on the last SIO module ie. MR-52, install the jumper across both PINs on J4. Starting with DIP Switches, some example address would be MR52 - Address 1 - SW1 ON , SW2 OFF , SW3 OFF , SW4 OFF , SW5 OFF MR52 - Address 2 - SW1 OFF , SW2 ON , SW3 OFF , SW4 OFF , SW5 OFF MR52 - Address 3 - SW1 ON , SW2 ON , SW3 OFF , SW4 OFF , SW5 OFF MR52 - Address 4 - SW1 OFF , SW2 OFF , SW3 ON , SW4 OFF , SW5 OFF MR52 - Address 5 - SW1 ON , SW2 OFF , SW3 ON , SW4 OFF , SW5 OFF Ensure the boards have been properly addressed is step one, step two is check that all MR52's have SW6 ON , SW7 ON , SW8 ON . 6,7,8 set baud rate. Above is an example of SIO Wiring from the LP1502 (Bottom Left) to each of the MR-52's. MR-52's are easily identifiable as having the bank of LED's at the top of the board. After checking that each board's dipswitches are set with correct address and baud rate and still have no 'B' LED activity, proceed to check the SIO wiring. This three wire connection should have a TR+, TR-, and GND. Each TR+ must be landed and daisy chained to the other MR52's TR+'s. If a TR+ on one board is accidently landed in a TR-, or GND it will kill the SIO communication. Its recommended to use separate colors for each termination for example all TR+ is RED, TR- is BLACK, GND is the unshielded silver ground in the case of shielded 22/2 or another color if using a different cable. If all the above checks out check voltage to the boards. If using a 12v source where the readers are configured for pass through power, its recommended that the power supply be capable of supporting up to 300Ma per connected reader. If using our LSP kit the power supplies spec'd are sized appropriately, this could potentially be an issue if using third party door kit hardware / power supplies. The input voltage on the MR-52 should be 10.8-13.2 vDC If using a 24 volt configuration the input voltage should be 22.8-25.2 vDC, and ensure the reader jumper next to the relays on the bottom right side of the board is set for 12v and NOT PT (Pass Through) or reader damage will occur. With OSDP reader deployments our standard when landing multiple readers to a reader port. Reader 1 must start with address 0 and the standard baud rate is 9600. Alternatively if landing one reader per port, the schema would still be the same the reader is addressed as Address 0, and Baud rate 9600.

t: Mercury and QxControl QuickStart Guide
d: Mercury QxControl Quickstart
b: Version: 1.1 | Created: November 2024 This guide covers adding a Mercury LP1501 or LP1502 controller to QxControl and configuring its doors. Before you begin: set the controller's IP address first. See Set Mercury Controller IP . QxControl Prerequisites – Places and Schedules Make sure Places, Schedules, and at least one Group and Permission are configured before you continue. You'll need "Areas" representing the non-secure and secure sides of the doors you're adding. In QxControl, the non-secure side is called Goes From and the secure side is called To . The simplest example is "Outside" and "Inside". See Places, and setting your Scope if you haven't set these up yet. Once this is complete, you're ready to add the device to QxControl. Mercury Configuration Follow these steps once networking is configured: Browse to the Gateways page. Select the Gateway the Mercury controller is connected to. Select Discover Devices . Click the Actions button and choose Mercury Scan . Your Mercury device should appear in the list if networking is correct on both the device and the Gateway. If it doesn't show up, see Mercury Hardware Tips and Tricks and Set Mercury Controller IP . Check the Mercury device and click Select Devices in the upper right corner. Click the Needs Config text on the right side of the screen. Verify the model, choose the reader protocol (usually Wiegand) and click OK . Click Add Devices at the top right. Browse to the Devices page on the left-hand menu and find the Mercury device you just added. Click it and select Edit Device . Add any connected boards (ex. MR52) if needed. Add Doors: Name the door. Associate a camera if relevant. Select an Unlock Schedule (the times the door is unlocked by default). Choose the From and To Areas based on your Places configuration. Access time defaults to 5 seconds. Adjust it if needed to change how long the lock stays open after a swipe. Select the correct door contact normal state (usually Normally Closed). Add your Reader (if applicable): give it a name for ease of use, and select the Place this reader grants access to. Add your REX (if applicable): give it a name, select the Place this REX grants access to, choose the default state (open or closed), and enable PIR Bypass if needed. Add your Lock : give it a name, choose the mode (Relay Opened or Relay Closed = Unlocked), and add a delay time if desired. Choose the SIO these are wired to. Select Close . This saves automatically. Click the Config button and then Update . Need help? Contact Qumulex Support at support@qumulex.com or 317-207-0520. Related articles Mercury Panel Initialization LP1501/02 Connection Troubleshooting How to update Mercury Controller Firmware

t: Mercury Hardware Tips and Tricks
d: Mercury Tips and Tricks
b: Version: 1.0 | Created: November 2024 Hardware settings and wiring tips for Mercury LP1501, LP1502 and MR52 boards used with QxControl. LP1502 Remove the paper sticker from the battery and set jumper J19 to ON . All DIP switches should be in the Off position. LP1501 Has an integrated battery, so there is no J19. Has a 4-position DIP switch block, which comes all On by default. After the IP is set, all 4 must be Off for normal operation. J3 must be set for PoE or 12 VDC operation. DIP switch 4 should never be On for Qumulex. It converts the board to a legacy device (EP1501), which is not compatible with QxControl. If the IP is already programmed and you need to reach the webpage, DIP switch 1 enables the factory username and password. To also revert the board to its default IP, set switches 1 and 2 to On. Switches 3 and 4 are always Off. TB2 can be used either as a reader port (LP1501 Reader support mode) or for an SIO board, when LP1501 Serial Support is selected as the device type in QxControl. Serial Support wiring: TB2-4 is Data 1 / TR+, TB2-5 is Data 0 / TR-, TB2-6 is GND. MR52 / LP1501 Reader Wiring (Reader Support mode) TB Pin TB Label Farpointe Wire Color Pin 1 VO Red Pin 2 LED Brown Pin 3 BZR Blue Pin 4 CLK White Pin 5 DAT Green Pin 6 GND Black MR52 Use 3 wires for the data connection, including the ground. The ground is required. The board address is set in binary on the first DIP switches: Address 1 = switch 1 On; Address 2 = switch 2 On; Address 3 = switches 1 and 2 On. DIP switches 6, 7 and 8 must be On for QxControl. This sets serial communication to 38,400 BPS with encryption on. Make sure the last serial device in the communication chain is terminated. The very last board may need jumper J4 for termination, though this is rarely needed. LED B goes solid when connected. If something isn't right, it slow-flashes about every 3 seconds. The board may need a reboot once it's connected and the DIP switches are set. If communication polarity is reversed anywhere, it can stop communication for the entire chain. When everything is working, LED B flashes rapidly when you scan a badge. This is a good way to confirm which board a reader is landed on. All controller connection statuses are shown under Wiring Info on the device page in QxControl. Example DIP Switch Assignments and Pinout This example shows an MR52 addressed as board 1, with two doors terminated to it. It assumes a door position switch (DPS), REX and reader at each door, with outputs landing on the LSP C4/C8 lock modules. MR52 Address 1 (DIP switch 1 On) MR52 Terminal Connection Input 1 Door 1 DPS Input 2 Door 1 REX RLY 1 Door 1 output to C8 #1 Input 1 Reader 1 Door 1 Input 3 Door 2 DPS Input 4 Door 2 REX RLY 2 Door 2 output to C8 #1 Input 2 Reader 2 Door 2 Need help? Contact Qumulex Support at support@qumulex.com or 317-207-0520. Related articles LP1501/02 Connection Troubleshooting QXEP-LP1501 I/O Example Wiring Mercury Panel Initialization

To do this navigate to Control Panel > Network and Internet > Network Connections. Select the interface that is connected to the Controller's Network. Select Properties on the Ethernet interface. Use an IP address such as 192.168.0.253 with a subnet mask of 255.255.255.0 Click Ok (Step 2) Open a web browser from a Laptop or Computer connected to the same network as the QXEP Controller. To enable the default credentials. User name: admin , Password: password flip the onboard dipswitch 1 to ON. Login using the default user name and password. If you plan on administering or updating the Controller via Go to Webpage in the future, now is a good time to set a user name and password to access the controller without having to flip dip switch one physically in the future. Navigate to the Users tab and create a user and password. (Step 4) After Login, Click on Network Click on the toggles to ' Use Static IP Configuration: ' and set the IP address to match the Gateway IP Schema. Click Apply Settings from the Left Side menu. Click ' Apply Settings, Reboot ' - At this point you will need to flip Dip Switch 1 on the LP Controller back to OFF Adding MR52-S3B / MR50 Reader Interface Boards to QXEP Controllers: This guide assumes the boards are powered up, and RS-485 Daisy chain is starting from the controller to each MR board in the enclosure. To establish communication with MR-XX boards, each board must be uniquely addressed starting with address 1, and the baud rate set. In the example above, for address 1, dip switch 1 is set to ON Dipswitch 6, 7, 8 are set to ON for 38,400 BPS and Encrypted Communication. The Chart above references address 1 through 6. t: Modify your localhosts for Offline Mode
d: For context see KB https://www.qumulex.com/kb/gateway-offline-access This KB will detail instructions on making per computer (and user) changes to your localhost file for using Offline Access on your
b: This article covers adding your Qumulex Gateway to a computer’s hosts file , so that computer can reach the Gateway during an internet outage. It’s needed for each computer (and OS user) that may need offline access. For the full Offline Mode setup, see: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/gateway-offline-access Before you start, copy or download the DNS List from Settings › Offline Access in QxControl. Each entry is one line: the Gateway’s IP address, a space, and its Hostname. Ex: 192.168.1.240 qx750010.qumulex.io Windows Press the Windows key and type Notepad Right-click Notepad and select Run as administrator In Notepad, click File › Open and browse to: C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\ Change the file type dropdown from Text Documents (*.txt) to All Files , then select hosts and click Open Paste the DNS List entries at the bottom of the file (example below) Click File › Save . Make sure it saves as hosts , not hosts.txt . Open Command Prompt and run ipconfig /flushdns to clear the DNS cache Mac OS Open Terminal Type sudo nano /etc/hosts and press Return Enter your Mac’s admin password Use the arrow keys to move the cursor below the existing entries Paste the DNS List entries from QxControl Press Ctrl + O , then Return to save Press Ctrl + X to exit Type sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder and press Return to clear the DNS cache Testing Open a browser and go to the Gateway’s Hostname (ex. https://qx750010.qumulex.io ). If the page loads, the hosts file is working. You can do this while the Gateway is still online. Note: if the Gateway’s IP address changes, these entries must be updated on every computer. That’s why we recommend a DHCP reservation or static IP for the Gateway. Related articles Setting up Offline Mode with Qumulex: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/gateway-offline-access Gateway IP Settings: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/qxgateway-static-ip

t: My Gateway is not showing online in the Cloud.
d: Gateway, Offline, Cloud
b: Verify and try these steps in order: Are there lights on the connected Network plug(s) on the back of the Gateway? If there are no activity lights, try another port in the switch or possibly a different patch cable. Be sure that IF you are using both network adapters, they are connected in a way so as to get different subnets for each NIC. Often that is achieved by manually setting the LAN network configuration, alternately you could use separate DHCP switches (or VLAN's). Make sure that the WAN network port is connected to a switch that has internet access, and that the network it is connected to is serving DHCP addresses. If steps 1-3 have been verified, the next step is to temporarily disconnect the LAN port from the back of the Qumulex Gateway. This will eliminate any chance of configuration conflicts. Once that is removed give the system a maximum of 10 minutes to resolve the cloud connection. If it is not up by then, it may be worth a restart of the unit with only the WAN cable connected. You can do this via a momentary press of the button on the front of the machine. It will automatically begin the power-down sequence, this will take up to 2 full minutes to complete. Once the lights and fans turn off you can power back up with another momentary press of the front power button. If the restart does not solve the problem it may be best to reach out to technical support via the phone. Note: If you are using an On Premise (not cloud) system another connection issue could be port forwarding, please see the following KB for details on that: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/port-forwarding

t: My Gateway went offline and won't come back. What can I check on site?
d: Gateway offline
b: Use this when a Gateway that was working is now offline. Answer each question, and each answer tells you which step to go to next. Start at Step 1. Step 1: Is the Gateway powered on? Look for power lights on the front and listen for fans. Yes, it's on → go to Step 3 No, it's off → go to Step 2 Step 2: Get power back Gateways power back on by themselves when power returns after an outage. If it's still off, check upstream first. Check the UPS, power strip, breaker, or remote power outlet. Momentarily press the front power button once. It powers on. Wait up to 10 minutes, then if still offline → go to Step 3 It won't power on, or turns on and shuts off → contact support Step 3: Check the network link lights Check the lights on the network port(s) in use. See What do the light colors mean on my Gateway Network Plugs? . No lights: try a different switch port and patch cable, then re-check Orange speed light on a gigabit switch: swap the cable or port. See Why is my network adapter at 100Mbps? Lights look normal → go to Step 4 Step 4: Does the WAN network have internet? Plug a laptop into the same switch port or VLAN as the Gateway's WAN . Does it get an address and reach the internet? No. The problem is the site's network or internet. Bring in the site IT team or ISP → done Yes, and the Gateway's LAN port is also plugged in → go to Step 5 Yes, and only WAN is plugged in → go to Step 6 Step 5: Rule out a WAN/LAN conflict Unplug the LAN cable and wait up to 10 minutes. It comes back online. The ports are conflicting (e.g. same subnet, or both with a default gateway). Fix them with Gateway IP Settings , then plug LAN back in → done Still offline. Plug LAN back in → go to Step 6 Step 6: Does “Go To Webpage” still work? In QxControl go to Gateways › Config › Go To Webpage . The login page opens. Something (usually a firewall or content filter) is blocking the cloud connection. Have site IT allow outbound UDP 51820 . See What ports do I open for my Qumulex Cloud Gateway? → done It doesn't open → go to Step 7 Step 7: Did anything change on the network? Yes (firewall, ISP, DNS, IP range). A Gateway with static IP or DNS settings on its WAN can't get out once those change. Update them with Gateway IP Settings . The qadmin login is on the sticker that shipped with the unit. Then → go to Step 8 Nothing we know of → go to Step 8 Step 8: Restart the Gateway the right way Momentarily press the front power button. Don't hold it. A safe shutdown can take up to 2 minutes. When the lights and fans are off, press it again. Wait up to 10 minutes for it to reconnect. Pulling the power cord can damage drives or recordings, so only do it as a last resort. See How do I power down my unit? . Back online → done . Set up a Gateway Offline alert so you hear about the next one first. Still offline → contact support Other situations Status says “Pending Version Update” . It is waiting to install an update. Leave it on and connected, and don't restart it. Contact support if it lasts more than a few hours. People need to use the system while it's offline. See Setting up Offline Mode with Qumulex (must be set up beforehand). It keeps going offline again and again for extended periods , while nothing else on the network does, or you seem to be missing recordings → contact support. Contact support Have ready: the Gateway serial number (on the label, e.g. QF2534P102FD), when it went offline, what the lights look like, which steps you've tried, and the site IT contact.

t: Places, and setting your Scope
d: Prominently within the QxControl software, you will find the Places section. What is a place? The places tree is a multi-level hierarchy of places. Imagine the root structure of a tree, Qumulex is
b: Prominently within the QxControl software, you will find the Places section. What is a place? The places tree is a multi-level hierarchy of places. Imagine the root structure of a tree, Qumulex is at the top, then integrators see their account, and underneath the integrator are their customers, and below that the customer’s sites and areas. The hierarchy is used to determine what a user of the software can see. This is then paired with the user’s role which defines what a user can do. It is this combination of what and where that defines a user’s ability to operate in the software. There are four types of places Integrator: The customer of Qumulex that sells and installs security systems Customer: Customer of the integrator, where the security equipment is installed, i.e. End User Site: A physical location for a customer. Used if the customer has multiple locations Area: A secured area for access control and also a logical intermediate level in the hierarchy Scope Every user is assigned to a place in the places tree and can see everything located at that place and any place below. To make managing a large system or multiple customers easier, use scope. Setting scope limits what is shown in the application to the place selected and anything below that place. This can be done from the Places page by selecting a point in the places tree and clicking Set Scope under the Actions menu. Alternatively you can use the Blue rectangle on the top right with the crosshairs icon. This will allow you to either dial in and set your scope to a more specific location, or clear your scope and set you back to the highest tier available for the currently logged-in user. Example: If my scope looked like this normally: And I wanted to specifically look at things at any of my customer "Bob's Bramble Shop" locations I would highlight the appropriate icon and select Actions and Set Scope as shown below: Once I have done that I will ONLY be able to see and have access to systems/cameras/doors that are beneath that Place in the hierarchy. As shown below. You will notice I no longer see the other customers. To reset my scope I simply click the blue rectangle scope button on the top right and click Clear Scope. Then I will be instantly back to seeing everything my user has permissions to.

Customer Preparation Browse to https://app.qumulex.io using Chrome, Firefox or Edge, and log in with your Integrator credentials. Select Places from the left-hand menu. Click Actions and then Clear Scope . If this Customer already has a Place created, skip to step 5. Otherwise: Highlight your Integrator name at the top of the tree. Click Create Place . Make sure the Parent Place is your Integrator and the Type is Customer . Type in the name of the customer (ex. School System) and add the timezone if known. Click Create Place . Locate the new system in the Places tree under Unassigned Gateways . It is named using the PO number given to Qumulex for this customer job. The icon looks like buildings, and may be green or red depending on the Gateway's current connection status. The next steps can be completed regardless of status. Select Actions and Enable Place Dragging . CAUTION: Be very careful in this mode. Drag the Site with the correct PO name and hover it over the new (or existing) Customer. Release it, and the Site and Gateway move automatically. You should receive confirmation that the transfer completed within a few seconds. IMPORTANT: Once this is complete, click Actions and then Disable Place Dragging . Set your scope to the new Customer/Site. This makes sure settings changes only affect this location. Highlight the new Site under the Customer in your Places tree. Click Edit Place and rename the Site to something relevant to the installation. Fill in any of the optional information. Example of a Customer and Site hierarchy: You can now create any of the following if needed. This can also be done later in the process. Areas – Created in the Places section. Mainly used for Access Control to define physical areas (ex. "Inside" and "Outside"). They can also define logical areas to organize cameras (ex. "Floor 1" and "Floor 2"). People – Add anyone who needs access to the system. Add credentials if this person needs access control permissions. Assign a Role if this person will use the QxControl software directly. Groups – Logical groups of people who need one or more common permissions to a Place. Schedules – Restrict the times people can access Places (Access Control). Permissions – A combination of Group, Schedule and Place that defines who can access Doors, and when. Camera Preparation Specific settings vary by manufacturer. We suggest a physically separate network switch for the cameras, connected to the LAN port of the Gateway. Use static IP addresses, or reserved DHCP addresses, for the cameras. This avoids video loss when an IP changes. Discover each camera's IP address using ONVIF Device Manager or the manufacturer's tool. Browse to the camera in a supported web browser. Set the basic camera parameters to fit the customer's needs: IP address and credentials Motion settings – not all cameras have motion turned on by default! Video streams (some cameras have a separate ONVIF stream setup, such as Axis): A high-resolution H.264/H.265 stream for recording A secondary, lower-resolution H.264/H.265 stream for live view bandwidth management Time zone/DST – synchronize to the Gateway if possible, otherwise set it to match local time. The time must be correct for the camera to connect. For more detail, see Camera Best Practices . Install-time Setup Gateway Connection Connect the LAN port of the Qx Gateway to the private physical security network at the site. Connect the WAN port of the Qx Gateway to the customer network with internet access. Plug the Qx Gateway into AC power and press the power button on the front (it may be behind a hinged door). Make sure your laptop is on the customer network with internet access. Software Setup Browse to https://app.qumulex.io and log in with your QxControl credentials. Find the customer Site matching the name you set above. You may need to clear your scope to see it. Highlight it and click Actions and then Set Scope . Wait for the Site icon to turn green (around 5 minutes). Both network ports are set to DHCP from the factory. If the LAN or WAN needs a static IP: Browse to the Gateways page under Configuration and click the Gateway you are configuring. Click the Config button and choose Go To Webpage . Follow the Gateway IP Settings article. Add Cameras Browse to the Gateways page under Configuration on the left side. Select the Gateway the cameras are being added to. Select Discover Devices . By default this runs an ONVIF scan, which should find all ONVIF-compatible devices within the available network. If nothing shows up, check your network settings from the earlier steps. Check all the devices you want to add and click Select Devices . In the shortened list, click the exclamation point next to Needs Config on the right side. Name the camera and enter its credentials. Click Next and repeat for each device you are adding. IMPORTANT: When you're finished, click the green Close button, then be sure to click Add Devices at the top right. Browse to the Cameras page and make sure every camera shows a green connected icon once the connection completes. To verify motion is being recorded, look for a blue border around the video during a motion event in Live. Create Views Go to the Live page and click the grid icon in the upper right. Select Layouts and choose your preferred layout. Select Widgets and drag any combination of cameras, widgets and doors into your layout. Click the views icon and type in the view name. Click Save as New View . Optional: to show a view automatically when Live opens, open the Views tab on the right, find the view, click the kebab menu (3 dots) and choose Set as Default for X . Need help? Contact Qumulex Support at support@qumulex.com or 317-207-0520. t: QxControl IT Guidelines
d: IT Guide
b: Version: Rev 1.4 | Created: January 2, 2026 This article explains how a Qumulex Gateway communicates with your devices and the Qumulex cloud, and which network endpoints and ports it needs. Share it with the site's IT team before installation. Operational Mode QxControl Operational Communications Architecture Device Communication Your Gateway communicates with security devices on your premises (ex. cameras, door controllers) over an IP network. Qumulex Gateways have at least two network interfaces. We highly recommend using one interface as a private network for your security devices. Keeping them isolated reduces exposure to vulnerabilities, and the Gateway acts as a firewall between those devices and the larger corporate network or internet. Cloud Communication Because QxControl is a cloud-enabled service, the Gateway communicates with several cloud-based services: Configuration and Status (Gateway) – The Gateway receives its configuration from the Qumulex cloud and sends status and events back to it. Users normally send and receive configuration and status through the Qumulex cloud, not directly to the Gateway. These messages travel over a secure WireGuard VPN, which is built into the Gateway's Linux kernel. On boot, the Gateway opens a UDP connection to wireguard.qumulex.io on port 51820 . WireGuard encrypts the data, but doesn't hide the underlying network protocols. Ports and addresses of Qumulex cloud services may be visible through packet inspection, but they are secure and shouldn't require extra firewall changes. Configuration and Status (Camera-to-Cloud) – Camera-to-cloud works much like Gateway mode. Because WireGuard isn't available in the camera's kernel, it uses Tailscale, a different implementation of the WireGuard protocol, to connect each camera to a Qumulex cloud endpoint. From the camera, QxControl finds the Qumulex Tailscale endpoint using STUN, reaching out to ICE servers at *.tailscale.com over UDP port 3478 . QxControl on the camera then opens an outbound UDP connection on port 41641 to the Qumulex Tailscale endpoint. Video recorded to the cloud – Video from cameras with a cloud recording subscription is queued on the Gateway. As bandwidth allows, and following any upload schedules you set, it is sent over HTTPS to upload-production.qumulex.io . Video transfer – Live and recorded video is sent on demand from the Gateway to the user's browser using WebRTC. WebRTC uses Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE), with STUN and TURN servers, to try to set up a direct peer-to-peer connection between the Gateway and the browser. The Gateway connects to the ICE server (normally coturn.qumulex.io ), then makes an outbound UDP connection to an address and port the ICE server provides. Depending on the network between the Gateway and the browser, WebRTC may fall back to a relayed connection. A direct peer connection is usually faster with lower latency. A router with full-cone NAT at the Gateway site is preferred. DNS – If the QxControl cloud can't be reached (ex. an internet outage), users may need to connect directly to the Gateway with the QxControl web app. This must use secure HTTPS, so Qumulex keeps a DNS record of the Gateway's public and private IP addresses. The Gateway finds its address by calling checkip.amazonaws.com , and the addresses are then updated with our DNS provider. Maintenance Mode Qumulex automatically keeps your Gateway's software up to date, so you have the latest security fixes and features. Make sure the Gateway's network doesn't block these updates: Software updates are downloaded from Google Container Registry and Google Artifact Registry. The Gateway must be able to connect to and download from us-docker.pkg.dev , gcr.io and us-central1-docker.pkg.dev on port 443 . Gateway software updates cannot go through an HTTPS proxy that uses a custom trust store (HTTPS interception). The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency has noted that HTTPS interception weakens TLS security . Qumulex tests and installs security updates for the Gateway's operating system (Ubuntu Server). The Gateway needs access to the Ubuntu package repository at archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/ . Our software continues to improve, and future versions may connect to new services. For the best experience, avoid non-standard HTTP blocking and content filtering. Summary of Endpoints and Ports End Point Port Protocol Direction wireguard.qumulex.io 51820 UDP (WireGuard) Outbound *.tailscale.com (camera-to-cloud) 443 TCP Outbound Qumulex Tailscale endpoint (camera-to-cloud) 41641 UDP (WireGuard) Outbound coturn.qumulex.io 3478 UDP (STUN/TURN) Outbound WebRTC peer — UDP Bi-directional upload-production.qumulex.io 443 HTTPS Outbound checkip.amazonaws.com 80 HTTP Outbound us-docker.pkg.dev 443 HTTPS Outbound gcr.io 443 HTTPS Outbound us-central1-docker.pkg.dev 443 HTTPS Outbound archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/ 80 HTTP Outbound Related articles What ports do I open for my Qumulex Cloud Gateway?
