t: QXEP-LP1501 I/O Example Wiring
d: How to wire and initially configure the QXEP-LP1501
b: The above example panel drawing shows a two input, one output, single Wiegand door reader configuration, with directly connected 12Vdc power. Panel Overview Upon un boxing ensure J3 settings are set for the correct power input for the application. J3 power selector jumper allows PoE or 12v directly wired power source via TB4-3 12vdc / TB4-4 GND. The above tables show a full explanation of Terminal and Jumper descriptions. Example Reader Configurations Input Circuit Wiring Typically, these inputs are used to monitor door position, request to exit, lock monitors. Input circuits are configured as unsupervised and consists of only open or closed states. Relay Circuity Wiring Two Form-C contact relays are provided for controlling door lock mechanisms or alarm signaling devices. The relay contacts are rated at 2A @ 30Vd, dry contact configuration. Each relay has a Common pole (C), a Normally Open Pole (NO), and a Normally Closed Pole (NC). When controlling the delivery of power to the door strike, the Normally Open and Common poles are used. When momentarily removing power to unlock the door, as with a mag lock, the Normally Closed and Common poles are used. Check with local building codes for proper egress door installation. Initial Configuration The four switches on S1 DIP switch configure the operating mode of the LP1501 Controller. DIP switches are read on power-up except where noted. When installing the LP 1501, it is important to ensure that its done in a secure manner. Upon installation, the user accounts to the web configuration page should be created with secure passwords, and all DIP switches are in the OFF position for the normal operation mode. The LP1501 is shipped from the factory with a default login account, which is enabled when DIP switch 1 is moved from OFF to ON. The default login user name and password will be available for five minutes once enabled. Therefore, it is important that at least one user account is defined, and the DIP switches are set to off before the LP1501 is commissioned. Its also highly recommended not to configure the LP1501 with an IP address that is accessible from the public internet. These devices should remain securely behind the physical barrier the Qumulex Gateway provides with all Access and Camera Devices behind the LAN network interface and the WAN interface being the only outside connection to the QX Gateway / Security Devices. Bulk Erase Configuration Memory The bulk erase function can be used for the following purposes: - Erase all configuration and cardholder database (sanitize board) - Update OEM default parameters after OEM default parameters after OEM code has been changed. - Recover from database corruption causing the LP1501 controller to continuously reboot.

t: Rosslare 825-IP and QxControl QuickStart Guide
d: Rosslare QxControl Quickstart
b: Version: 3.0 | Created: May 20, 2026 This guide covers preparing QxControl, then adding and configuring a Rosslare AC-825IP controller with its doors. QxControl Prerequisites 1. Places Set your Scope Navigate to Places on the left-hand menu at https://app.qumulex.io . Highlight the appropriate Customer Place. Select the Actions menu and then Set Scope . This makes sure all of your work stays in this location. Set your Timezone From Places, click each Customer and Site in your scope. If the timezone is incorrect, click Edit and correct it. Create "From" and "To" Areas Areas represent the physical spaces at the site. Swiping at a door and opening it moves a person from one Area to another. Create at least two Areas under your Site, for example "Outside" and "Inside". You can add to or change these later. Click the Site name in the Places tree (the icon is green or red). Click Create Place and type Outside for the name. Click Create Place to save it. Select the Site again and repeat, typing Inside for the name. 2. Groups and Permissions You need at least one Group and one Permission to configure doors. If you don't have them yet, create a basic placeholder so you can finish setup: Browse to Groups from the left-hand menu. Click Create Group . Give the Group a name (a generic name is fine). Select the Site from the Place dropdown and click Create Group . Browse to Permissions from the left-hand menu. Click Create Permission . Choose the Site from the Place dropdown. Choose the new Group from the dropdown. Choose the Always schedule. For more complex Groups and Permissions, see Using Groups . 3. Networking Qumulex Gateways have two network ports. Most commonly, the WAN connects to the internet using DHCP, and the LAN connects to the security device network (usually a static IP). See Gateway IP Settings if you need to configure this. You can also use only the WAN port if you choose. Connect the Rosslare 825-IP panel to the same switch and network as the Qumulex Gateway, on either the LAN or WAN side depending on your setup. Once this is complete, you're ready to add the Rosslare 825-IP to QxControl. Rosslare 825-IP Configuration Browse to the Gateways page. Select the Gateway the Rosslare 825 is connected to. Select Discover Devices . Click the Actions button and choose Rosslare Scan . Your Rosslare 825 should appear in the list if networking is configured correctly. Verify the firmware is AC825V05_00_03 or newer. Check the Rosslare 825 and click Select Devices in the upper right corner. Click the Needs Config text on the right side of the screen. Enter the Device name, and a description if desired. Type in the IP address you want the 825 set to. Important! This sets a static IP exactly as typed. Be sure the address is correct and not already in use. Click OK . Click Add Devices at the top right. Browse to the Devices page on the left-hand menu and click the Rosslare 825 you just added. Select the Edit Device tab at the top. Choose the Device Protocol: Standard (Wiegand) or OSDP , depending on the cards and readers in use. Choose the Device Configuration: 1 Reader Per Door or 2 Readers Per Door . Note: The Device Configuration can't be changed later without reconfiguring the doors, so make sure you choose the right one. Click Save Device . Wait at least 60 seconds while the Device populates its information. It automatically adds a template for your doors, which you'll fill in next. Let this complete. Click the Edit Device tab again. You should now see a number of Doors (likely highlighted red) below the main device configuration. Click the first door to open its configuration screen. Rename the door to something meaningful. Choose an Unlock Schedule (this can be changed later). Most often this is Never for a door that stays secure 24/7. Select a From (ex. "Outside") and a To (ex. "Inside") for this door. Configure your Reader : name it if desired; choose the Access type (Card and PIN is the default); select the Primary Card Format (usually 26-bit H10301 for standard low-frequency cards); optionally choose a Secondary Card Format if the site uses more than one type of card. Configure your REX : name it if desired; select the Place this REX grants access to; choose the Default State (normally open or normally closed). Configure your Lock : name it if desired, and pick the Lock Mode (see the Lock Relay Mode Reference below). Click Next at the top left and repeat for each door. Note: Every door must be configured, even if you don't plan to use it yet. Fill in at least the required fields marked with a red asterisk. When finished, click the green checkmark at the top left, next to the Next button. Scroll down and click the green Save Device button at the bottom left. Your Device should now show an orange exclamation mark in its status at the top right. Click Config and then Update . Watch the Panel State indicator in the upper right turn green when configuration is complete. Lock Relay Mode Reference Choose the lock mode based on how the lock is wired: Lock Type Relay Setting Behavior Normally Closed Relay Open = Unlocked Circuit opens to unlock Normally Open Relay Closed = Unlocked Circuit closes to unlock Configuration Notes Card Formats: 26-bit (H10301) is the standard for low-frequency cards. Use the Secondary Card Format to add other formats if the site uses other card types. Door Contact Settings: Select "Normally Open" if the door sensor is open when the door is secure (most common), or "Normally Closed" if the opposite applies. OSDP Defaults: Doors 5–6 use OSDP with addresses 13 and 14 respectively, and a default baud rate of 9600. Firmware: Qumulex supports firmware AC825V05_00_03 or newer. If the Version field is blank during discovery, the controller is running unsupported firmware and must be upgraded first. Access Time: Defaults to 10 seconds. Adjust it in the door editor to change how long the lock stays unlocked after a valid swipe or command. Verifying Your Configuration The Rosslare device should show green and Connected on the Devices page. Test each door: Select Doors from the left-hand menu. Click the door you want to test. Click the red Unlock button. The door should unlock temporarily. Swipe a badge on that door's reader. The badge number should appear in Recent Events , matching the site code and card number of the badge. Repeat for each wired door. Need help? Contact Qumulex Support at support@qumulex.com or 317-207-0520. Related articles How to Configure the Rosslare 825 with QxControl (video) Places, and setting your Scope Using Groups

t: Rules Overview
d: Simply put, Qumulex Rules give you the ability to configure various triggers within our system to execute an action or actions. The first release will allow you to trigger notifications such as Email
b: Simply put, Qumulex Rules give you the ability to configure various triggers within our system to execute an action or actions. The first release will allow you to trigger notifications such as Email or SMS. In the future the function of rules will expand well beyond the function of a notifications tool. When creating a rule you can stack a number of Triggers using "if, then" statements and "and, or" paramaters. For example: IF I get a status of CrossLine on my system THEN I want an email. The breadth and depth of what can trigger a notification can vary widely. These can be linked to schedules, limited to certain places, filtered to only happen if multiple events occur at the same time, and if the event happens for a certain number of seconds consistently, just to name a few. I will link several KB's up with examples of these configurations.

t: Setting up Offline Mode with Qumulex
d: If a Qumulex Gateway loses internet access, you can still connect and use the system using one of the following methods. This will allow you to connect and view the Gateway from the Local Network whi
b: Setting up Offline Mode with Qumulex If a Qumulex Gateway loses internet access, you can still log in and use the system from the local network. Everything below must be set up before the internet goes down. Setup has two parts: A way to sign in offline: a Passkey (Option A) or an Offline Password (Option B). A way to reach the Gateway on the local network: DNS or hosts file entries (Steps 2 and 3). This is required for both options. Option A: Passkeys (simplest) A passkey is tied to your device and works whether the system is online or offline. See: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/how-do-passkeys-work-in-qxcontrol If you use a passkey, skip Step 1 and continue with Steps 2 and 3. Option B: Offline Password Each user who may need offline access creates their own Offline Password (Step 1). During an outage, the user must be on the same local network as the Gateway. Who can create an Offline Password? Offline Passwords can only be created by users at the Customer level or below . An Integrator/Dealer user, set at the Integrator level, cannot create one, even when scoped to the customer. Setting Scope only changes what you see. It doesn’t change which user you’re logged in as. If the customer wants their Dealer to have offline access: The customer’s administrator creates a Person for the Dealer at the Customer level (or below), using the Dealer’s email address. The person needs a Role so they can log in. This step is done by the customer, not the Dealer. The Dealer switches to that user. In QxControl, click your name in the bottom left and select the customer-level user from the list. This switches your login to that user’s profile, which is different from setting Scope. The Dealer creates the Offline Password while switched to the customer-level user, by following Step 1 below. During an outage, the Dealer signs in with that email and the Offline Password, the same as any other customer user. Step 1: Create your Offline Password This is done per user, and only for users at the Customer level or below (see Who can create an Offline Password? above). If you haven’t created one yet, you’ll see an Action Required icon next to Settings . Click Settings , then select Offline Access Click Create Password . This takes you to the password section at the bottom of the page. Enter and confirm your Offline Password, then click Create Offline Password Be sure to remember this password. It cannot be reset while the Gateway has no internet connection. While the system is online, you can change it from the same page. Before Step 2: Set a DHCP reservation or static IP for the Gateway. The DNS and hosts entries point to the Gateway’s IP address, so if it changes, offline access will stop working. See: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/qxgateway-static-ip Step 2: Get the Gateway DNS list Go to Settings › Offline Access and scroll to Configure Host and/or DNS Server Confirm your Scope is set to the correct customer or site. Use Reset Scope or Change Scope if needed. This matters most if you’re an Integrator configuring on behalf of a customer, or if there’s more than one Gateway at the location. See: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/setting-your-scope Click Download DNS List , or Copy to Clipboard , to get the Name, IP and Hostname of each Gateway at your current Scope. The Hostname (ex. qx750010.qumulex.io) is the address you’ll use to reach the Gateway when offline. If you see “No data for table”, your current Scope doesn’t include a Gateway. Adjust your Scope, or contact your system administrator. Step 3: Configure DNS or hosts files Choose one of the following: Local DNS server (preferred): have the site’s IT team add each Hostname and IP from the list to the local DNS server. This works for every computer on the network. Hosts file (per computer): add the entries to the hosts file on each Windows or Mac computer that needs offline access. See: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/modify-your-localhosts-for-offline-mode Logging in during an outage From a computer on the same local network as the Gateway, open a browser and go to the Gateway’s Hostname shown in the DNS list (ex. https://qx750010.qumulex.io ) Sign in with your Passkey , or with your email (or username for LDAP) and your Offline Password Testing Offline Mode You can test the offline login while the Gateway is still online. Once Steps 1–3 are complete, go to the Gateway’s Hostname (ex. https://qx750010.qumulex.io ) from a computer on the local network and sign in with your Passkey or Offline Password. If the page loads and you can sign in, your DNS or hosts setup and your password are working. To fully confirm it works during an actual outage, the Gateway has to be offline. If you want to run this test, plan it with the site and disconnect the site’s internet connection temporarily. Keep the Gateway connected to the local network so the computers can still reach it. Related articles How do passkeys work in QxControl: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/how-do-passkeys-work-in-qxcontrol Modify your localhosts for Offline Mode: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/modify-your-localhosts-for-offline-mode Gateway IP Settings: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/qxgateway-static-ip

t: Unified Door Kit Wiring Four Door Kit QXEP-DKUF-04DR-1502-U
d: Wiring the Qumulex QXEP-DKUF-04DR-1502-U Door Kit, Mercury
b: The above panel drawing is High Resolution, for more detail, you can zoom in with CTRL+Mousewheel to view terminations and board markings. Overview of Wiring: In this diagram the FlexIO (Yellow Cable) daisy chains between all the component boards to provide fault and Fire Alarm Interface through the system. System power is provided by the three wire buss connectors provided with the Door Kit. The blue, orange, black wire harness can be connected using the soldered spade connectors on the modules shown in the drawing. Blue is 24v, Orange is 12v from the B100, and Black is the ground. Output 1 on the D8 to TB4 on the QXEP-LP1502 provides Class 2 12v power as required by Mercury. Components: FPO75 - Provides 24v @ 3A. The output is selectable between 12/24V by the two position jumper in the center of the unit. The FPO 75 will charge 4 to 40 Ah of battery capacity. B100 - is responsible for stepping down the 24v from the FPO75 to provide 12v system power. Input power for the B100 is derived from the FPO75 which is set for 24v. D8 - Provides 8 protected DC outputs for use by the QXEP system. each individual voltage output zone may be programmed for a continuous output or to respond to a fire alarm interface for control of egress locks at one of the two system voltages. C4 - The C4 lock controller module provides 4 access control inputs capable of voltage or dry contact activation. Each lock output is programmable to either 12v or 24v DC. QXEP-LP1502 - Qumulex Access Controller powered by Mercury. Supports 2 Doors Directly attached, with 4 readers, 8 inputs, 4 outputs. Component Settings: B100 - The JP3 on the B100 should be set to Position 1 from the factory, and what Qumulex recommends. Setting the jumper JP3 to position 2 allows an adjustable output range from 5 to 18Vdc using the VR1 on board potentiometer. D8 - Has selectable jumpers on each output labeled JP1 through JP8 and are used to select the output voltage for each output in dual voltage systems such as this kit. Position 1 selects 24v, Position 2 selects 12v. D8 Output 1 needs to be set for Position 2 for the QXEP-LP1502 prior to power up. Its best practice to meter check the voltage output from the D8 output prior to installing the TB4 connector on the QXEP-LP1502 to ensure all upstream devices have been wired properly. t: Using 2FA with QxControl
d: QxControl may be configured to use third-party authenticator apps as your second source of authentication. If enabled, you'll be required to provide a code supplied by your selected authenticator app
b: QxControl may be configured to use third-party authenticator apps as your second source of authentication. If enabled, you'll be required to provide a code supplied by your selected authenticator app when you log in. To initiate 2FA, you'll scan the QR code from within QxControl ( https://app.qumulex.io/qx/settings/authentication ) and provide that to your third party authenticator app, e.g. Google Authenticator , LastPass Authenticator , Microsoft Authenticator , etc. After that, when you log in to QxControl, you'll need to provide a code that is supplied by your authenticator app. Another way to log in is by using the one-time-use backup codes that were generated when you enabled 2-factor authentication. These are presented to you immediately after you set up 2FA with your authenticator app. Ensure you save them in a secure location to use in case you lose access to your authenticator app. Subject to your organization's rules, users may disable 2FA on their account at any time after they are logged in. Finally, Qumulex can disable two-factor authentication on your behalf. To do so, we will need you to verify your identity for security purposes. You will need to contact support@qumulex.com and be able to present a government-issued ID and have access to the account's email address.

t: Using Groups
d: Groups Permissions Doors
b: Use Groups to organize physical access to Places In QxControl, Groups are used for organizing access to physical locations, i.e. Doors . Groups are assigned Permissions , which means the People who are members of the Group can get access to a Place (and its children Places) on a defined Schedule . All Doors that provide access to that Place are subject to the Permission . Note : Because Groups are only relevant to physical access control, it is recommended that only People who have access control credentials are included in Groups. There are alternate ways to manage access for People who are able to log in and use QxControl software. To ensure visibility and control by Customers over who can access their Places, QxControl has the following limits: Access control credentials can only be assigned to People whose home place is at the Customer level or below. Note : If an integrator's technician needs access to a customer's place, simply create a Person (without a Role) within the customer's hierarchy and assign a credential. Credential uniqueness is only enforced within a customer, so the technician's same credential can be used for all customers at which access is required. Permissions, and the Groups to which they pertain, can only be created for Places at the Customer level or below. Subject to a Customer's choice, Integrators may have visibility and configuration capability for their Customers; however, they can not create People or Permissions that give access to a Customer Place that is hidden from the Customer. The how-to video below shows the steps to create Groups and Permissions.

t: Verify the integrity of a saved clip export
d: Watermarking integrity
b: Ensure a downloaded clip has not been modified When a Clip is saved in QxControl, the backend Clips service copies the video footage recorded either on the gateway's hard drives on in cloud storage buckets and packages it into an MP4 file which is stored in a dedicated, secure cloud storage location until it reaches its expiration time. There is no access to this MP4 file to modify it's contents while it is in the cloud. If the MP4 file is downloaded via the QxControl UI, this file becomes accessible to all manner of video editing tools that could modify its contents. You can verify the integrity of a downloaded version of your clip by comparing the MD5 hash ( https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MD5 ) of the downloaded file against that of the MP4 file in the cloud. First, obtain the MD5 hash of the cloud clip. To do this, press download on the Clip You will be shown a dialog that contains the MD5 hash. Press the clipboard icon to copy the hash value. Next, go to an online MD5 calculator, e.g. https://md5file.com/calculator and compute the hash for the file you want to verify. If the hash values match, the downloaded MP4 file has not been modified since the clip was generated.

t: What cameras do you support?
d: Qumulex support h264 streams from all cameras using ONVIF Profile-S or Profile-T. For further information please see our Supported Products page. (h265 is not supported)
b: What camera models do you support? Qumulex supports cameras that conform to ONVIF Profile S , along with Profile T and Profile M . QxControl connects to the camera’s H.264 or H.265 video streams over Profile S. When a camera also supports Profile M, QxControl can use its analytics metadata for features such as attribute search. To check whether your camera is supported, search your make and model on the ONVIF Conformant Products page: https://www.onvif.org/conformant-products/ . Compare the firmware version ONVIF lists as tested with the firmware on your camera. Cameras often need a firmware update before they connect properly. Camera requirements ONVIF Profile S conformant, with ONVIF turned on in the camera. Some manufacturers ship it turned off. H.264 or H.265 encoding on the streams you plan to use. Best Practice is at least two streams: one high resolution and one lower resolution, with the same aspect ratio. Qumulex records the high-resolution stream and uses the lower one for mobile and multi-camera live views. Motion or analytics events set up in the camera. Qumulex uses the camera’s own events to trigger recording. Some cameras ship with motion detection turned off by default, so check the camera’s web page and enable it if needed. Optional: ONVIF Profile M, for analytics features (see below). Note on H.265: Viewing H.265 video requires a browser and computer that can decode HEVC. If you see a message about H.265 when viewing live video, see: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/error-using-h265-video Additional features Some cameras offer extra functionality in QxControl beyond standard ONVIF video and events. Feature availability depends on the camera’s make, model and firmware. ONVIF Profile M: cameras that support Profile M and classify people and vehicles can be used with Analytic Search (clothing color, vehicle type and similar attributes). This requires the QXP-A license. See: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/analytic-search Camera to Cloud: lets supported cameras connect directly to the Qumulex cloud without a Qx Gateway. See: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/what-ipro-cameras-work-with-qumulex-camera-to-cloud Known exceptions A few camera models have specific firmware or settings requirements. Before a large install, check: Devices with known Firmware requirements: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/known Camera Best Practices: https://www.qumulex.com/kb/camera-best-practices Before rolling out a large install, connect a single camera first to make sure it works with your setup. For the full list of supported devices, access control hardware, and integrations, see our Supported Products page: https://www.qumulex.com/supported-products

t: Why do some live video frames lose video?
d: There are several possible issues that can cause the live video feeds to issue a reconnect command. The first thing to know is that reconnecting a live stream does not necessarily mean there will be
b: There are several possible issues that can cause the live video feeds to issue a reconnect command. The first thing to know is that reconnecting a live stream does not necessarily mean there will be anything wrong with the recording. In fact in most cases they are completely unrelated. The most common and basic is if we do not receive a valid frame for 15 seconds from the camera we will drop the live stream and attempt to reconnect. This can be as simple as network throughput/connectivity. Sometimes these problems can come from camera settings. The most foolproof way to ensure this is not the case would be to factory default the camera and reconnect to see if it cleared up your live viewing issue. Alternately you may be having live display issues due to your GPU. Either being to slow, or possibly just a processing issue. The first test for this would be to turn off GPU acceleration within your browser.

t: Why is my door not following its schedule?
d: Door not following schedule
b: Answer each question, and each answer tells you which step to go to next. Start at Step 1. Step 1: What is the door doing? Unlocked when it should be locked, or locked when it should be open → go to Step 2 Shows locked in QxControl but is physically unlocked, and locks when a card is swiped → go to Step 7 The door is fine, but certain people are denied with “NotPermittedAtThisTime” → go to Step 8 A gate opens or closes on its own → go to Step 9 Not sure what changed it → go to Step 10 Step 2: Is the door in a manual override? Hover over the door's lock icon. An overridden door uses the same icon as a normal unlocked door, so only the hover text tells you. Hover text says Overridden (e.g. “Lock: Overridden Unlocked”). Someone used Unlock or Lock, and it stays that way until released. → go to Step 3 It doesn't say Overridden → go to Step 3 anyway. Reverting is quick and safe. Step 3: Revert to schedule Select the door, click Actions , then Revert to Schedule . The door goes back to normal → done . After any temporary unlock, use Revert to Schedule. Still wrong → go to Step 4 Step 4: Check the door's schedule Go to Doors , pick the door, click Edit Door , and look at the Unlock Schedule at the top. Wrong schedule selected: pick the correct one (or Never ) and save → done Right schedule, wrong hours: fix its time blocks under Schedules → done Right schedule and hours, but the door runs hours early or late → go to Step 5 Only happens on or around a holiday: check the Holiday Set on the schedule. See Setting up Holiday Schedules → done All of this looks right → go to Step 6 Step 5: Check the Place's time zone Schedules run on the time zone of the door's Place. A missing or wrong time zone shifts everything (e.g. opening at 12:15 AM instead of 7:15 AM). Set it with How do I set my timezone in Places . Fixed → done Time zone is already correct → go to Step 6 Step 6: Make sure the controller has the latest settings Schedule changes only take effect once they reach the door controller. Check that the door's controller shows Connected . Use Update Panel on the controller by clicking Config and Update from the door or Device, then Actions › Revert to Schedule on the door. If the controller shows an update error or never finishes updating, contact support (see below). Sometimes one bad record can stop the rest of a controller's settings from downloading. Mercury controller keeps dropping offline? See LP1501/02 Connection Troubleshooting . Step 7: Lock polarity is reversed Follow Lock Status appears to be the opposite of the physical door . Step 8: People are denied, but the door is fine This isn't the door's schedule. People get access through their Group , and each Group's Permission sets which Places they can enter and on what Schedule . Open the person in People and check which Groups they're in. Open that Group's Permission and check its Schedule. If it's a holiday, the holiday has to be defined on that schedule too. See How do I give someone door access? and Using Groups . Step 9: A gate moves on its own Check the door activity in QxControl for the time the gate moved. There's an event at that time. QxControl most likely moved the gate → go to Step 2 No event in QxControl. The gate operator likely moved it on its own (its own timer, loop detector or inputs). Check the operator's settings and wiring with your installer → done Step 10: Find out what changed the door Run a door activity report for the time of the issue. It shows unlock/lock commands, schedule changes and access events. Check the Audit Trail for changes to Doors, Schedules, Schedule Blocks or Holiday Sets. Then start again at Step 1 with what you found. Still not working? Contact support Include the Gateway serial number and door name, the date and time it happened (with time zone) , what the door should have done vs. what it did, whether anyone used Unlock, Lock or Revert to Schedule, and a screenshot of the door's activity for that time.

t: Why is my recorded video missing, freezing, or not exporting?
d: REcorded video, freezing, not exporting, clips issues
b: Answer each question, and each answer tells you which step to go to next. Start at Step 1. Step 1: What are you seeing? The timeline has gaps, or no colored bars where you expected video → go to Step 2 First, zoom in. If you're viewing a full day or week, the bars are only an estimate and can show gaps that aren't really there. Zoom in to 6 hours or less and check again. The timeline shows bars or motion events, but the video won't play → go to Step 5 The video plays but buffers, freezes, or jumps → go to Step 6 A problem creating, downloading, or sharing a Clip → go to Step 8 Step 2: Is the camera connected right now? Check the camera's icon on the Cameras page. Not green (disconnected or “unsupported”). The camera can't record while it's disconnected, so gaps line up with the time it was down. See Camera Connectivity Tips . If every camera on the Gateway is affected, see My Gateway went offline and won't come back . Tip: set up Creating a Camera Disconnect email alert in Rules so you hear about it right away, not when you need the video. Green → go to Step 3 Step 3: Is the camera recording motion events? Most cameras record on motion, so no bar on the timeline can just mean nothing moved. Check that motion detection is turned on in the camera, has at least one motion zone, and has sensible sensitivity. Some cameras ship with motion turned off. See Camera Best Practices . Motion was off or the zone was wrong: fix it in the camera → done The event icon says “no events” but you think the camera is recording: check the Search page for that camera's events → done Motion is set up correctly and gaps still appear while things are moving → go to Step 4 Step 4: Check the camera's stream settings These settings cause most recording gaps: Turn off any “smart” or dynamic encoding (Smart Codec, AI Codec, Dynamic GOP or Dynamic Frame Rate). Dahua has its own article: Dahua Starlight camera stops recording . Set the GOP to at least twice the frame rate. Update the camera to its latest firmware. Sync the camera's time to the Gateway. Then reconnect the camera in QxControl. Gaps stop → done Gaps continue → go to Step 7 Step 5: Bars show on the timeline, but the video won't play You're zoomed out too far (for example, a full day or week). At that zoom the bars are only an estimate of where video exists, so a click can land on a spot with no video. Zoom in to 6 hours or less and click inside a bar again → done The footage is older. It may only be in the cloud now. In the Timeline, click the cloud icon ( Play Video From Cloud ) → done The error mentions H.265 or HEVC.
